references.text: Jesus warns the disciples that they will be handed over to councils and brought before governors and kings for his sake – a direct parallel to Luke 21:12 ([ref:Matt 10:17-18|Matthew 10:17-18]).

Mark's version of Jesus' eschatological discourse contains the same warning about persecution, being handed over to synagogues and prisons, and standing before kings and governors for the sake of Jesus' name ([ref:Mark 13:9-11|Mark 13:9-11]).

Jesus tells the disciples that a servant is not greater than his master, and that those who persecuted him will also persecute them – a fundamental prediction about the persecution described in Luke 21:12 ([ref:Joh 15:20|John 15:20]).
Jesus predicts that the disciples will be expelled from synagogues, which corresponds to being handed over to synagogues mentioned in Luke 21:12 ([ref:Joh 16:2|John 16:2]).

Peter and John are arrested and thrown into prison by the temple leaders – an early fulfillment of Jesus' words that they would lay hands on the disciples and persecute them ([ref:Apg 4:1-3|Acts 4:1-3]).
The apostles are again arrested and put in public prison, in accordance with Jesus' prediction about persecution and imprisonment ([ref:Apg 5:18|Acts 5:18]).

King Herod lays hands on some in the church, kills James, and puts Peter in prison – a clear fulfillment of being brought before kings and imprisoned for the sake of Jesus' name ([ref:Apg 12:1-4|Acts 12:1-4]).
Paul is brought before King Agrippa and governor Festus, which directly fulfills Jesus' words about being brought before kings and governors for his name's sake ([ref:Apg 25:23-24|Acts 25:23-24]).
Paul defends himself before King Agrippa, a concrete fulfillment of the prophecy in Luke 21:12 about being brought before kings ([ref:Apg 26:1-2|Acts 26:1-2]).

Jesus predicts that the disciples will be handed over to tribulation and put to death, and hated by all nations for his name's sake – a parallel to the persecution mentioned in Luke 21:12 ([ref:Matt 24:9|Matthew 24:9]).
Jesus tells the church in Smyrna that they will be thrown into prison and experience tribulation, which reflects the theme of persecution in Luke 21:12 ([ref:Åp 2:10|Revelation 2:10]).
